# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

20:pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
21:
22:- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
23:  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
24:  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
25:  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
26:- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
27:  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
28:- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
29:- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
30:- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
31:- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
32:
33:### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
34:
35:The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
36:
37:`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
38:
39:```yaml
40:# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
41:# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
42:validate:
43:  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
44:  next: load
45:load:
46:  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
47:  next: apply
48:apply:
49:  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
50:  govern: [ transaction ]
51:  next: save
52:save:
53:  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
54:  govern: [ transaction ]
55:  next: respond
56:respond:
57:  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
58:```
59:
60:```java
61:// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
62:public class ValidateOwner {
63:  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
64:    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
65:  }
66:}
67:public class LoadOwner {
68:  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
69:      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
70:    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
71:    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
72:    ownerOut.set(owner);
73:  }
74:}
75:public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
76:  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
77:    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
78:    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
79:  }
80:}
81:public class SaveOwner {
82:  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
83:    repository.save(owner);
84:  }
85:}
86:public class RespondWithOwner {
87:  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
88:    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
89:  }
90:}
91:```
92:
93:`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
94:
95:```yaml
96:handle:
97:  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
98:```
99:
100:```java
101:public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
102:  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
103:      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
104:    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
105:  }
106:}
107:```
108:
109:### Step wiring
110:
111:Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
112:point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
113:method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
114:`method:`.
115:
116:- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
117:  as `@Parameter T`.
118:- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
119:  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
120:  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
121:
122:### Function parameters
123:
124:Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
125:
126:- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
127:- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
128:- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
129:  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
130:  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
131:- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
132:  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
133:
134:### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
135:
136:Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
137:into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
138:
139:- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
140:- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
141:  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
142:- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
143:  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
144:
145:### Naming
146:
147:Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
148:absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
149:publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
150:`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
151:
152:Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
153:responder. Steps in between work with entities.
154:
155:### Request body and validation
156:
157:- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
158:  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
159:  first step publishes it as a variable.
160:- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
161:  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
162:  invalid body can return 400.
163:
164:### Transactions
165:
166:`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
167:listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
168:the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
169:
170:### Errors
171:
172:Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
173:Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
174:`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
175:`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
176:anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
177:
178:### Security
179:
180:Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
181:
182:```yaml
183:composition:
184:  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
185:```
186:
187:- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt

content.text:
Roles and the clerk limit are in, and all 4 acceptance scenarios pass on the first `bin/e2e` run.

**How settling works now**
- A clerk can settle a claim only if its due is at or below the sheet's clerk limit. Above the limit, the server refuses and the claim row shows the error.
- A claim whose due is n/a is always within the limit.
- Stewards can settle anything.
- The opener still can't settle their own claim; that check runs before the limit check.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V18__settings.sql`, adds a nullable `clerk_limit` column to `sheet` (blank means no limit) and a `sheet_role` table. Any name without a row there is a clerk.

**Server:** a new `settings` package with three endpoints:
- `GET /api/sheets/{id}/settings`
- `POST /api/sheets/{id}/settings` sets the clerk limit, which must be blank or 0.00 or more with up to two decimals. It writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=clerk-limit value=<limit>`, even when the value hasn't changed — the test expects that.
- `POST /api/sheets/{id}/roles` assigns a role. Anything other than `clerk` or `steward` (e.g. `boss`) is refused. It writes `ROLE_SET … user=<name> role=<role>`.

The limit check itself is in `ChangeClaimStatus.java`.

**Front end:** a new settings panel in `features/settings/` has:
- the clerk-limit form, showing the limit currently in force
- the role form
- a list of the roles set, using the `data-testid` names the test expects

The test helper fills an optional "from" date field for a setting if the screen has one. I left that field out because the request doesn't call for dated settings, so the limit always applies from the moment it's saved.
